description: We are Team Smart Watchers, a multidisciplinary team passionate about combining space technology, environmental science, data analysis, and interactive learning.. We are interested in connecting with participants who are passionate about coding, data analysis, Earth science, remote sensing, UI/UX, game development, and creative storytelling.
summary: In order to promote sustainable agriculture, Eco-Eye is an interactive geospatial platform that combines field-based soil measurements, environmental data, and satellite views. In addition to comparing agricultural regions and investigating possible water and salinity stress, it allows farmers and researchers to track vegetation health, soil moisture, salinity, and land surface temperature. Additionally, the portal enables researchers to export data for scientific analysis, submit their own soil measurements, and compare them with indicators collected from satellites. Eco-Eye seeks to enhance knowledge of agricultural conditions, facilitate well-informed irrigation and crop-management decisions, and enable more resilient and sustainable farming in dry regions through field validation in Bidiyah, Oman.
details:
1. Executive Summary

Satellite data can tell us a great deal about the land, but turning that information into something useful on a farm is not always straightforward. Eco-Eye was developed to make that process easier. By bringing together space science, remote sensing, field observations, and artificial intelligence, the platform aims to turn complex data into clear agricultural insights and practical guidance in Arabic. In this way, it can help farmers and researchers make better-informed decisions about the land and its resources.

Users can select a farm or compare two agricultural sites and explore ten environmental and agricultural indicators. These include root-zone soil moisture (with a target depth of up to 40 cm), soil salinity, heat and water stress, and drainage quality. The results are presented on an interactive map, using colors to make differences between areas easier to understand. Users can also divide a farm into smaller field sections, ask the contextual AI assistant, Eco-Bot AI, for support with plant-related problems, and explore suggestions for suitable crops and irrigation plans. Data can be downloaded in CSV format for further analysis.

Ultimately, Eco-Eye is intended to help users make more informed choices about irrigation, recognize areas that may be at risk of salinity or land degradation, and consider crops that are better suited to local conditions.

2. Project Background and Challenge

Satellites regularly collect information about the Earth's surface, including vegetation, soil moisture, temperature, and rainfall. This information is valuable for agriculture, but it is not always easy for farmers or local researchers to use. The data may come from different sources, use different formats, and require technical knowledge before they can inform a practical decision.

Eco-Eye brings these different sources together in one place. Rather than asking users to interpret separate datasets on their own, the platform presents relevant indicators through a single map and dashboard. The aim is to make the information easier to explore and to connect it with decisions that matter in everyday farm management and agricultural research.

3. Project Description and Proposed Solution

Eco-Eye is an interactive digital platform designed to help users monitor agricultural land and identify conditions that may need attention. It brings together satellite and geospatial information in a map and dashboard, allowing users to focus on one farm or compare two locations.

Key Features

· Choose a farm on the map, or select two farms to see how their conditions differ.

· Explore ten environmental and agricultural indicators, such as root-zone moisture, soil salinity, heat stress, water stress, and drainage quality.

· View land conditions through a simple color system: green for more favorable conditions, yellow for areas to monitor, and red for areas that may need closer assessment.

· Break a farm into smaller sections to see how conditions vary from one part of the site to another.

· Use Eco-Bot AI for contextual support with plant-related questions and suggestions for crop choices and irrigation planning.

· Export the data as a CSV file for use in further analysis, reports, or research.

4. Environmental and Agricultural Indicators

To build a clearer picture of conditions across a farm, Eco-Eye brings together several environmental and agricultural indicators. The main indicators include:

Indicator

Purpose within the Platform

Root-zone soil moisture

Estimate water availability in the root zone, with a target depth of up to 40 cm as specified in the project description.

Soil salinity

Identify indicators associated with salt accumulation and areas that may require specific soil-management practices.

Water stress

Highlight indicators of water deficiency or insufficient water availability for plants.

Heat stress

Monitor thermal conditions affecting plants and land, including conditions associated with evaporation.

Vegetation health

Assess vegetation density and the condition of plant growth.

Drainage quality

Analyse soil characteristics associated with water infiltration and drainage.

Rainfall

Track precipitation to support the assessment of water resources.

Soil properties

Use spatial soil information to understand differences in soil characteristics across an area.

Land suitability indicators

Combine indicators to provide a simplified spatial overview of site conditions.

Spatial and temporal comparison

Compare locations or monitor changes in indicators across available time periods.

5. NASA Data Sources and Geospatial Datasets

Eco-Eye uses a combination of satellite and geospatial datasets. Each source contributes a different type of information to the overall analysis. The table below outlines how the project team intends to use each dataset:

Data Source

Use within the Project

SMAP

Soil-moisture data, supporting the assessment of moisture conditions relevant to the root zone.

ECOSTRESS

Thermal infrared data and plant-temperature observations to support the monitoring of heat stress and evapotranspiration.

NDVI

A vegetation index used to assess vegetation density and the condition of plant growth.

GPM

Precipitation data for tracking rainfall and supporting the assessment of water resources.

SSURGO

Soil-property data supporting the assessment of drainage quality and soil permeability.

LANDSAT

Multispectral bands and imagery used to analyse soil and vegetation characteristics and indicators associated with water stress and salinity.

6. How the Platform Works

1. Site Selection: The user selects an agricultural plot on the map or chooses two locations for comparison.

2. Data Retrieval: Relevant available satellite and geospatial data are collected for the selected location.

3. Indicator Analysis: The data are processed to generate environmental and agricultural indicators in a unified format.

4. Results Visualization: Results are displayed through the interactive map and dashboard, with the option to explore sub-fields.

5. Recommendations and Export: Users can access contextual recommendations through Eco-Bot AI and export the data in CSV format.

7. Beneficiaries and Expected Impact

· Farmers: Support irrigation and farm-management decisions, as well as crop selection, using site-specific indicators.

· Researchers and universities: Provide spatial data and indicators that can support agricultural and environmental studies.

· Agricultural and water-resource authorities: Support planning, monitoring, and the identification of locations that may need assessment or intervention.

· Educational communities: Make remote sensing and Earth-science applications in sustainability more accessible.

Expected Impact

· Promote more efficient irrigation-water use by improving understanding of site-specific water conditions.

· Support the monitoring of soil-salinity risks, land degradation, and desertification.

· Help identify crops that are better suited to local environmental conditions.

· Make satellite data more accessible through an interactive Arabic-language interface.

· Strengthen data-informed agricultural decisions rather than relying solely on general estimates.

8. Scientific Basis and References

The development of the project indicators and the understanding of remote-sensing applications in precision agriculture were informed by previous scientific studies on soil-moisture and soil-salinity monitoring, the integration of radar, optical, and thermal data, and the use of machine-learning techniques in agricultural land analysis. The following references were provided by the project team:

1. Al-Mulla, Y., Al-Mahrezi, K., Al-Hammadi, M. S., Ali, A., & Parimi, K. (2025). Remote sensing techniques for detecting soil salinization from 1985 to 2021 in hot and hyper-arid Saham Basin, Oman. International Journal of Agriculture and Biosciences, 14(2), 209–222. https://doi.org/10.47278/journal.ijab/2024.211

2. Dong, L., Wang, W., Che, T., Wang, Y., Huang, X., Zhang, S., Xu, F., & Feng, J. (2025). Agricultural Water Management, 312, Article 109410. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.agwat.2025.109410

3. Guo, Y., Ding, J., Wang, J., Zhao, D., Tan, J., Qin, S., Wang, R., Zhao, S., & Guo, J. (2026). Precise inversion of soil water-salt and management zoning for oasis cropland in arid regions. Journal of Environmental Management, 412, Article 130224. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.130224

5. Rawat, M., Nguyen-Huy, T., Sena, D. R., & Ali, A. (2026). Advances in remote sensing techniques for surface soil moisture estimation: A systematic review of recent developments (2019–2024).
